VERDICT: PASS
BLOCKING: none
MINOR: bench/instruct/checks.py (ABBREVIATIONS) - `no.` is treated as an abbreviation, so a mid-answer sentence such as "The answer is no. It is not." counts as one sentence instead of two, which can wrongly pass or fail the sentences check in cases 04, 09 and 14.
MINOR: bench/instruct/score.py (classify) - an `is_error` result with non-empty text is graded as an answer and can FAIL, which contradicts "errors excluded"; this holds only if the provider ever puts error text in `answer`.
MINOR: bench/instruct/run.py (call_failed) - a provider refusal that returns `is_error` false with an empty answer is scored as FAIL, not ERROR; this depends on how bench/coder/run.py sets `is_error`, which is not in the diff.
MINOR: bench/instruct/test_instruct.py (test_sentences_real_model_style) - the comment calls the sentence "the real Haiku answer", but it is hand-written and not tied to the saved run file, so the claim is unverified.
MINOR: bench/instruct/run.py (CR.SYSTEM, CR.CFG) and bench/instruct/test_instruct.py (RunScript.run_main) - run.py mutates shared coder-module globals, and the test sets BENCH_CLAUDE and BENCH_CWD without restoring them, so state leaks between tests.
MINOR: bench/instruct/cases.json (case 20) - the prompt says at most 25 words but the check uses `max_words` k 27 to allow for the two markers; the README does not explain this.
MINOR: bench/instruct/cases.json (case 14) - the prompt "do not use any of the characters * # ` or _ ." is ambiguous about whether the period is banned; the check only bans `*#`_`.
